entries.fact: DIFF = Previous - Current. VAR = DIFF / Previous. When Previous is zero, VAR is unavailable. Grand-total VAR uses grand-total DIFF divided by grand-total Previous.
entries.source: Michael Goyone's reporting requirements

entries.fact: The uploaded example reports are layout references, not current sales data. New uploaded sales reports determine quantities and net sales.
entries.source: Michael Goyone's reporting requirements

entries.fact: MAX uses Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with Transformers.js and q4 weights. Browser model downloads/cache and available device memory affect startup; this is local inference, not model retraining.
entries.source: Qwen ONNX model card and Transformers.js v3

entries.fact: A browser may expose WebGPU but return no GPU adapter. MAX checks the adapter and falls back to WASM on the CPU if GPU setup fails. CPU inference may be slower.
entries.source: MDN WebGPU and Transformers.js WebGPU guide; MAX runtime implementation

entries.fact: Browser speech recognition has limited support and may send audio to the browser provider's service. Local MAX text inference does not make microphone transcription offline. Typing remains available.
entries.source: MDN SpeechRecognition

entries.fact: MAX tests a key by requesting the provider's model list. A saved connection is not proof that a paid generation will succeed; the requested model's permissions and API quota still apply.
entries.source: OpenAI model-list reference; MAX connection implementation

entries.fact: MAX's default cloud image model is gpt-image-2.5-sunburst through the Images API; it returns PNG image data. This is separate from the on-device text model and requires API access.
entries.source: OpenAI image-generation guide; MAX creation implementation

entries.fact: SpreadsheetML uses oddHeader/oddFooter on all pages when differentOddEven is false. MAX keeps a repeating grayscale report footer with MG/date and page numbers; its report paper options remain Letter, Legal and Ledger in either orientation.
entries.source: Microsoft Open XML HeaderFooter reference; owner print requirements

entries.fact: Printed footer paths are separate from the download location. Excel uses native Path and File fields. PDF uses the configured report folder and actual filename; CSV includes those values in Footer metadata rows because CSV has no page layout. The browser and user settings choose the actual download destination.
entries.source: MDN anchor download attribute; MAX Report Studio implementation

entries.fact: Excel headers and footers use Times New Roman; the body uses Aptos Display and categories use Aptos SemiBold. PDF embeds Liberation Serif, Liberation Sans and the OFL-licensed Source Sans 3 Semibold by default. Supporting browsers can request installed Times New Roman and Aptos fonts after the owner clicks Report fonts. Selected local font data stays on the device.
entries.source: Microsoft cloud font list, Adobe Source Sans license, MDN Local Font Access API; applied exporter

entries.fact: ProductMix filenames containing an explicit ISO start/end range identify PMIX reporting dates. Verified report headers also supply metadata; conflicting dates require confirmation. Preview and PDF download use the same document generator. Save report includes source data, filters, layout and header/footer settings in a private portable JSON file.
entries.source: MAX Report Studio source and owner reporting requirements

entries.fact: Report titles use 16-point bold; subtitles use 12-point bold with initial capitals per word and preserved abbreviations. All header/footer text uses Times New Roman; printed timestamps, path, filename, MG date and page numbers use 8 points. Printed timestamps have no timezone suffix. PDF embeds installed Times New Roman when authorized, otherwise the disclosed Times-compatible fallback. Body: 12-point bold ITEM/column and uppercase dining headings, 10-point semibold categories, 8-point regular items and numbers. Short reports use white body rows; dense reports use restrained light-gray shading. Native Excel headers repeat; overflowing filters continue in the legend.
entries.source: Microsoft Excel header/footer documentation; applied MAX report exporter

entries.fact: Carry-Out contains W/I Walk-In, C/I Call-In, ONL Online Order, D/T Drive-Thru, KSK Kiosk and DD DoorDash. Dine-In contains BAR, PATIO and DI inside seating. Catering contains CT-DEL delivery, CT-P/U pickup and CT-ONL online. Filters display only source-supported scopes. Menu-level Dine-In or Carry-Out totals cannot establish more detailed subtypes. The report legend explains used abbreviations; All Dining Options refers to all dining scopes present in the uploaded source.
entries.source: Owner reporting requirements; applied source-driven dining filters

entries.fact: Files with the same reporting dates automatically align locations side by side by item. Location display offers side-by-side columns, VS for two selected locations, or combined totals. Two matching-format files with different dates automatically select source VS; three or more select source columns. Earlier dates are Previous, with reversal available. Absent items in a complete loaded report show zero. Missing source values remain unavailable. Distinct intervals are not silently added.
entries.source: Owner reporting requirements; applied MAX comparison engine

entries.fact: For supported Toast All levels workbooks, MAX reads every tab and checks item detail against Summary, Items, Menus and Menu groups, excluding gift-card rows from item PMIX; modifier occurrences are checked against the Modifiers tab. A separate modifier quantity view uses actual modifier counts. Modifiers can overlap and are not unique item counts or item net sales.
entries.source: MAX workbook importer and reconciliation checks

entries.fact: All report formats use inches: top 0.85, bottom 0.75, left/right 0.25, header/footer 0.30. The report body aligns left at 0.25 inch; the title stays centered in the native Excel header. Header/footer use Times New Roman. PDF uses the installed font when authorized, with the existing embedded serif fallback.
entries.source: Owner reporting requirements; Microsoft custom margin documentation

entries.fact: Back to formats returns from the live document preview to the collection. The owner can add, edit, save, duplicate, delete and download reusable formats. Excel/PDF/CSV references supply structural layout measurements, not sales data. MAX can suggest constrained settings on the device; optional cloud assistance requires the owner to select paid API mode. Saved format definitions are owner-private and exclude report rows.
entries.source: Applied MAX format library and owner requirements

entries.fact: MAX embeds Jspreadsheet Community Edition 5.0.4 and jSuites 5.12.0, both MIT licensed. The editor supports worksheet tabs, cell edits, copy/paste, undo/redo, widths, row heights, font controls, grayscale shading and borders. Native XLSX parts and formulas are preserved in an edited download; formulas are not executed in the browser and recalculate in Excel. It is a focused workbook editor, not a complete Excel replacement. Reusable format settings can adopt selected cell styles without saving cell data.
entries.source: Jspreadsheet CE repository, license and installed runtime; MAX workbook editor

entries.fact: Category totals and grand totals each have independent Top/Bottom controls. One numeric column omits the duplicate right-side TOTAL; its location appears in the report header and its column is labeled QTY, NET SALES or VALUE. Multiple location columns retain their right-side totals. Comparisons retain separate source-period totals, and different dates are never combined. Subtotal and grand-total VAR use aggregate Previous and Current values.
entries.source: Owner reporting requirements and applied PMIX calculation/export logic

entries.topic: Visible app version and update details
entries.fact: Owner standard for apps: always show Version number, Build number, Updated date and Updated time with an explicit timezone. MAX shows these in its footer and PIN screen, with static build details available before the status request completes. Applied source changes update build metadata; public knowledge revisions increase only when knowledge changes are applied.
entries.source: Owner instruction and applied MAX interface

entries.fact: Excel native print footers use &Z for the file path and &F for the filename (shown in Excel as &[Path] and &[File]), followed by MG and the export date. PDF and CSV use the owner-configured report folder and actual filename. Browser download location is separate from the printed path.
entries.source: Microsoft Excel header and footer documentation

entries.fact: Private Google Drive file access requires OAuth authorization. MAX requests drive.file for files created by its connection. New uploaded originals and downloads up to 40 MB are archived privately; after owner connection, Drive copies are verified before staging bytes are removed. Unconnected or failed transfers remain pending in private MAX storage. Delete moves History entries to Trash and Undo restores them. No private files are stored in public GitHub. History provides separate Download original and Download generated report links, plus each generated file’s uploaded sources. The setup guide uses Google Auth Platform Branding, Audience, Data Access, and a Web application client with the exact /api/drive/callback redirect. External Testing authorization for drive.file expires after seven days. Client secrets must be copied at creation and stored privately.
entries.source: Google OAuth and Drive documentation; applied MAX History behavior

entries.fact: Automatic filenames place selected store abbreviations first in standard store order, followed by a short title, report year and MMDD_MMDD date range. Full product-mix reports use PMIX Full, without the redundant word Menu. Cross-year ranges keep both years; comparisons retain distinct source intervals. Single-store location codes stay in the native report header. Example: FX - PMIX Full 2026 - 0819_0825.xlsx. Explicit manual filenames remain editable.
entries.source: Owner reporting requirements and applied report metadata generator

entries.fact: MAX ZETA reads all workbook tabs. Explicit row-level Location/Store/Restaurant values are preserved for each item. A Summary that lists multiple stores with one merged Qty sold column is a combined-only source; listing stores is not an allocation of item quantities. Such exports remain labeled combined totals and cannot show individual-store VS. Overlapping combined and individual sources are rejected to avoid double counting. Missing item net sales are not inferred from Summary money.
entries.source: Applied importer and location-view logic; owner reporting requirements

entries.fact: The private reporting workspace and main-website report button are named MAX ZETA. MAX-G remains the separate AI companion. The existing owner account, private data and reporting URL are preserved.
entries.source: Owner naming instruction

entries.fact: MAX ZETA parses source reports, calculates quantities/net sales/comparisons, and generates Excel, PDF and CSV locally without OpenAI or Gemini calls. Its optional on-device Qwen assistant requires an initial model download; owner sign-in and private History still need internet. Files Uploaded counts distinct original files, not workbook tabs or dining groups. Clear / reset uploaded data clears the working report and queued imports while preserving History and saved formats. Undo reset restores the working session until another report is opened/imported, new files are uploaded, or the page reloads. Generated History entries link the current report’s original uploads.
entries.source: Owner requirements and validated application behavior

reviewLimitations: Toast Product Mix documentation could not be retrieved on 2026-09-12. Import changes were verified against supplied format examples and synthetic fixtures; they were not re-certified against current Toast documentation.
dailyReview: Daily documentation and sourced-knowledge review is enabled through Michael’s ChatGPT task. New knowledge is applied only when supported and validated. Model weights do not retrain.
